title: Inference Metrics — TTFT, TPOT, ITL, Goodput, P99

questions.question: Throughput reads 15,000 tokens per second, but users abandon sessions because many requests blow past two seconds. What metric is missing?
options: Longer timeouts so nothing ever fails
Per-request SLO attainment across latency axes
questions.explanation: Throughput cannot see abandoned sessions. This lesson defines TTFT, TPOT, percentiles, and goodput: did the user get what was expected.

questions.question: For RequestTrace, which terms make up ttft_ms in the local implementation?
options: Prompt tokens divided by output tokens
questions.explanation: The ttft_ms property returns queue_ms + prefill_ms; decode samples are added later by e2e_ms.

questions.question: A trace has TTFT 500 ms, 100 output tokens, and 700 ms total decode time. What does tpot_genaiperf return?
questions.explanation: GenAI-Perf excludes TTFT and divides the 700 ms decode sum by output_tokens - 1, so 700/99 is about 7.07 ms.

questions.question: For that same trace, what does tpot_llmperf report?
options: 7.07 ms because it starts at token 2
500 ms because TTFT is the only input
questions.explanation: LLMPerf's local method returns e2e_ms/output_tokens = (500 + 700)/100 = 12.00 ms, including TTFT.

questions.question: Why can high aggregate throughput coexist with poor goodput?
options: Aggregate speed can hide SLO misses
Throughput is always computed from P99 only
A request is good if any single token arrives
questions.explanation: Throughput sums output tokens over the fleet; goodput is a per-request all-constraints result, so fast aggregate work can still violate TTFT, TPOT, or E2E.

questions.question: Why does the lesson emphasize P50, P90, and P99 rather than only a mean?
options: Percentiles remove the need to define TTFT
The mean cannot be calculated for a list of traces
P99 is always lower than P50 in this simulator
questions.explanation: A small number of long-prefill or queue-spike traces can dominate user experience while barely moving the mean; percentiles expose those tails.
